title.purpose: Article H2, PT Serif 700 with a 1px bottom border.

body.purpose: Inter prose and section names; the reading floor, running the full width of the article column.

caption.purpose: Inter dense chrome: nav links, table bodies, section-row descriptions, news leads.

label.purpose: Mono 600 uppercase with 0.1em tracking: section labels, badges, dates, keyboard hints. Meta, never content.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: Quiet warm-tinted lift for low popovers; near-black at night (rgba(0,0,0,0.35)).

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Deep lift under the search results listbox, the one surface that leaves the page plane. Night: rgba(0,0,0,0.5).

shadows.name: fade
shadows.purpose: Edge shadow on a horizontally scrollable panel with more content past it (a clipped code line, the mobile TOC strip). Night: rgba(0,0,0,0.35).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Ease-out-quart; interactive transitions leave fast, settle soft.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Default duration for color, opacity and border-color state changes.

motion.name: hero-crossfade
motion.purpose: The home hero's four-background crossfade; starts once the page has loaded and slides 2–4 have downloaded; collapses to one still (and fetches one photo) under prefers-reduced-motion. No pause control, deliberately (owner's decision).

narrative.overview:
ES Doc is a field manual for Russian-speaking modders of the visual novel *Everlasting Summer* (Бесконечное Лето). The whole system lives inside the game's own light: warm afternoon sun on a sand path by day, and the deep blue of the lake at camp by night. It should feel like a senior modder left you good notes, warm enough to trust and precise enough to ship from. Content is the product; every color, border, and font exists to make text findable and readable, never to decorate.

The theme is genuinely bimodal, not a dark tool with a light afterthought. **Light is the default** (`prefers-color-scheme` chooses): cream paper under warm sun, ink-brown text, the pioneer-red galstuk (neckerchief) as the one spot of alarm-free warmth. **Dark is the night scene by the lake**: deep night-blue surfaces, warm-cream text, a lifted pioneer red that still passes AA as link color. Code panels follow the theme too: a sheet of print on the desk by day, film-dark by the lake at night — one syntax palette each, rather than one palette forced to serve both.

This system explicitly rejects the sterile autogenerated look of ReadTheDocs and Sphinx, the corporate gray of a Confluence wiki, and try-hard neon/cyberpunk gaming aesthetics. Familiarity is a feature here: modders know wikis, and nothing should surprise them except how warm it feels.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-tinted neutrals only; never pure `#000` or `#fff`.
Pioneer red is a once-per-screen spotlight, not a fill.
PT Serif carries the warmth in headings; Inter carries the body; Consolas signals meta and code.
Flat by default; the one shadow is the search popover lifting off the page.
Light and dark are equal citizens, switched by ambient preference.

rules.name: The Galstuk Rule
rules.body: Pioneer red appears on ≤10% of any screen. Its rarity is the point; a whole sidebar or a full row of red breaks it. Emphasis inside a red-tinted surface leans on weight, not more red.

rules.name: The Two-Palette Code Rule
rules.body: Code panels follow the theme like every other surface. That means two syntax palettes, not one: the ink weights on `#FDF9EE` by day, the lifted film palette on `#12161E` at night, each verified ≥4.5:1 against *its own* panel. Adding a `--code-*` token to one theme without the other is the same bug as any other half-defined token.

rules.name: The Tinted Paper Rule
rules.body: On light, a semantic wash is mixed toward white *first* and then laid on nearly opaque (92%); it is never a saturated hue at 8–16%. The paper is not a neutral — `#F4EAD6` is a yellow at chroma 11 — so a thin film of anything lands wherever that yellow drags it. The callout washes learned this the hard way: sky-blue info composited to hue 130° (a grey-green), forest-green tip to 102° (a khaki two degrees off the page), and all five callouts ended up inside one warm 50–130° arc, telling themselves apart by lightness alone and reading like panels borrowed from the night theme. Pre-mixing puts the hue back where it belongs (info 233°, tip 126°, attention 90°, warning 37°, danger 29°) and lifts the strongest band from L* 82–88 to 87–92 — a tint *on* the paper instead of a wash *over* it. Night keeps the thin-film treatment: a dark page is cool and neutral enough that a translucent hue stays the hue it started as.

rules.name: The Elevated-Surface Rule
rules.body: Accent text never sits on `--bg-elevated` at night: `#F2606C` on `#2A3142` is 4.12:1, under AA, where the same text on `--bg-surface` is 4.87. The footer's support control was built around this (it deliberately leaves its background alone on hover); the image lightbox was not, and shipped its «Открыть файл» / «Скачать» links under the bar for months. A panel that needs accent links keeps `--bg-surface` under them, whatever the surface above them does.

rules.name: The No Pure Neutral Rule
rules.body: Never `#000` or `#fff`, and never an untinted gray. Every neutral is pulled toward sand/ink warmth (or, at night, toward lake-blue). Prefer the token (`var(--ink)`, `var(--border)`) over any literal hex that has one.

rules.name: The Cyrillic-Leading Rule
rules.body: Headings led at 1.2 until it was measured: PT Serif 700 at 38.4px has a 51px font box, and a 1.2 line box is 46px, so two-line headings overlapped their own em boxes. Russian exposes what Latin hides — Ё and Й carry marks above cap height while у, р, ц, щ and д descend, which left 2.5px between one line’s descenders and the next line’s diaereses. Leading on this site is budgeted for Cyrillic, not for a ratio borrowed from Latin setting.

rules.name: The Hyphenation Rule
rules.body: Prose sets `hyphens: auto`, and `lang="ru"` on the document is what makes it work. At 375px a Russian paragraph runs about 30 characters a line, far under the 45 the eye wants, and the body size cannot come down to meet it. Hyphenation is the only lever left.

rules.name: The Serif-Carries-Warmth Rule
rules.body: Headings are ink-colored, not accent-colored. PT Serif carries the warmth so pioneer red stays a spotlight (see the Galstuk Rule). A page full of red headings is drift.

rules.name: The Three-Weight Rule
rules.body: Only 400, 600, and 700 exist. Weight 500 was removed from the scale; do not reintroduce it.

rules.name: The Measured-Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: A breakpoint sits where something measured stops fitting, and the stylesheet says what was measured next to it. Never a device width picked for its name.

rules.name: The Fixed-Header Rule
rules.body: The header, fixed to the top of the viewport, is one 52px row at every width at the default text size. Anything that would make it taller goes underneath it and scrolls. Nothing copies that 52px, though: the sticky sidebar and every scroll offset read `--header-h`, which follows the real header, so when a larger default text size does give it a second row, nothing slides underneath.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only when an element genuinely leaves the page plane, today that is the search popover alone. Cards, rows, callouts, and panels use borders and tint, never a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Picture-Gets-The-Curve Rule
rules.body: 12px belongs to things that are pictures of something — code, screenshots, artwork. A frame around text stops at 6px, and a list gets no frame at all.

dos: **Do** reach for the token, `var(--ink)`, `var(--border)`, `var(--accent)`, `var(--info)`, never a literal hex that has a token.

**Do** give every new color token both halves at once: a plain light value in `:root` and a `light-dark(day, night)` pair in the `@supports` block of `vars.css`. A token that exists in only one mode is a bug (this is exactly how the info callout was once broken).
**Do** keep pioneer red to a once-per-screen spotlight; use weight or size for emphasis inside warm surfaces.
**Do** give code panels a palette per theme, and verify each one against its own panel.
**Do** use PT Serif for headings/quotes, Inter for body/UI, Consolas for meta labels and code, at weights 400/600/700 only.
**Do** pair every callout/icon with `class="icon"` and `currentColor` so it inherits the semantic color and the shared 24px size.

**Do** keep the site's own links in the **same tab** — the nav, section rows, footer icons, and outbound rows like `/news/sources` and «Прочие ссылки»: no `target="_blank"`, so readers keep their back button and choose a new tab themselves (WCAG G200; NN/g; GOV.UK). The one exception is a link *inside an article's prose* that leaves the site: the markdown renderer opens it in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, because articles are reference material read while doing something else, and following the Ren'Py manual mid-example shouldn't cost the reader their place in it. Authors write both kinds the same way; the renderer decides. The other exception is hand-written, at the owner's request: the resource lightbox's «Открыть файл» opens the original beside the list, so the lightbox and the reader's place in a long listing survive the look.

**Do** use тире (`—`, U+2014) as the Russian title separator (`'Авторы — ES Doc'`) and nested-list marker. This deliberately overrides the English "no em dashes" default: the audience reads Russian, where тире is correct.
**Do** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: disable both transitions and keyframe animations, merged into one block per stylesheet.

**Do** underline links inside running text at rest — a faint `--link-underline` (half the link's own colour), full on hover and focus. Colour alone can't mark them: accent on ink is 2.83:1 by day and 2.44:1 at night, under WCAG 1.4.1's 3:1. Navigation, section rows and buttons read as links by place and shape and stay bare; footnote markers and code-labelled links carry their own cue.

**Do** keep every state visible in Windows' high-contrast mode (`forced-colors: active`), which drops shadows and repaints backgrounds: focus goes through `outline` (a transparent one where the design draws its ring with a shadow), the current page gets a `text-decoration` underline, the active search option the system `Highlight`.

**Do** draw icons that repeat down a long list with CSS (`.res-icon`: a data-URI mask filled with `currentColor`), not inline SVG — on the 1 162-row sprite listing, three SVGs a row were half the HTML and some 9 300 DOM nodes.
donts: **Don't** ship the sterile autogenerated **ReadTheDocs / Sphinx** look, the corporate gray of a **Confluence wiki**, or try-hard **neon/cyberpunk gaming** aesthetics (PRODUCT.md anti-references).
**Don't** use `#000`, `#fff`, or any untinted gray. Warm-tint every neutral.

**Don't** use `border-left`/`border-right` wider than 1px as a colored accent stripe on callouts, banners, rows, or blockquotes. Use a full border, a background tint, or nothing. (The sidebar's 1px `--border-tan` nested-nav indent is the only allowed structural exception.)
**Don't** add drop shadows to cards, rows, or callouts. The search popover is the only element that leaves the page plane.
**Don't** color headings with pioneer red; ink + PT Serif carries them.
**Don't** reintroduce font-weight 500, or a display font in UI labels/data.
**Don't** replace тире (`—`) in Russian copy with a colon, pipe, or middle dot.

**Don't** hand-write `target="_blank"` anywhere else — the renderer owns the prose case, and the lightbox's «Открыть файл» is the one written by hand — and don't add external-link/new-tab icons (NN/g and GOV.UK found they aren't reliably understood; GOV.UK removed theirs).

**Don't** add a pause or stop control to the home hero's crossfade. It was removed deliberately at the owner's request and is to stay out; `prefers-reduced-motion` is its off switch (see the hero under Components).
